newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Up on India but seen shortlived.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Up on India but seen shortlived.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil market rose on Friday on the back of India's award of 855,000 tonnes in its July tender, but traders expected the recovery to be shortlived amid plentiful supplies and as more arbitrage cargoes were expected to arrive.
Traders noted that the award into India's gas oil tender reflected lower Mediterranean prices which partly explained why the arbitrage from the Mediterranean to Singapore has reopened.
They calculated the spread between the two regions at just under $30 per tonne based on Singapore swaps values.
Traders noted that four tankers have been fixed for shipment from the Black Sea and Mediterranean, with some estimating the number to be as many seven to eight, due for arrival end-June/early July.
Traders said at current values, these cargoes would land in Singapore at parity to spot quotes.

But there was still a chance that these cargoes might be diverted elsewhere if stocks in Singapore remained abundant, as large volumes remained unsold from the previous flotilla of arbitrage shipments during March-April, amounting to three million tonnes.
Singapore middle-distillates stocks for the week June 28 ended was at a four hear high of 10.54 million barrels, according to the Trade Development Board.

But traders also noted that Singapore remained the best place to sell as a group of three traders continued to buy regularly at a rate of about two cargoes daily. The traders have so far bought about 22 million barrels since March 3.

On Friday, one of the buyers, a Japanese trader bought two cargoes from a Swiss trader--one cargo at $25.30 per barrel for June 14-18 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis and the second at $25.40 for June 25-29 lifting fob.
The trades were 50 and 10 cents respectively over Thursday's deals.
Swaps June gas oil gained 15 cents to be last quoted at $25.30/$25.35, and July gained 10 cents at $25.15/$25.25.
Traders said more sellers would emerge if swaps prices hit the $25.40-$25.50 mark, before sliding again.

Traders said jet fuel registered a remarkable recovery on Friday trading twice at $24.70 for June 25-29 between two European majors and at $24.55 for June 14-18 between a US trader and a European major.
Jet fuel broke the $24.00-mark on Thursday to trade twice at $23.85 and $23.90 per barrel, fob. Traders on Thursday had said that the traded values were much too low.

Sri Lanka had bought by tender gas oil at five cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and jet fuel at a 10-cent premium from Dutch trader Vitol for June 10-11 delivery, cost-and-freight Colombo.
